cells.tense: You are here at the setting down, and the people around you are meeting it.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Keep tending whatever you gave something up for — a small daily bit of care, the way you'd keep a fire you don't want to smother.
cells.core:
You set something down, and it got its answer. The people near you noticed what it cost, and that noticing is doing real work — it tells your body the offering landed somewhere instead of pouring into a hole. The setting down moves at its own pace because you're not forcing it, and they echo it back without needing a speech from you.

Underneath, this is plain care for what's still growing. Tend that on purpose: the thing you gave something up for, kept with a steady hand rather than clutched. That's the next step, and it holds whether the room keeps looking or not. You don't have to force the nod, and you don't have to earn it by giving more.
cells.sheetLine: What you set down came back as something the room could see.
cells.verb: setting down what was carried until the giving is seen and valued

cells.tense: The nod is still coming toward you from somewhere ahead, so you will wait inside yourself until it lands.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Sort what you're still holding for a nod from what you set down for its own sake, and keep only the second pile.
cells.core:
The setting down was real, but part of you is at the window waiting for the acknowledgment to arrive. You've made it conditional on somebody noticing, and the waiting has a tightness to it — you're still carrying what you thought you put down, because something in you is watching to see if it landed. The grip came back through the side door.

One careful look fixes the shape. Set out both piles: what you put down because it was done, and what you're holding only so someone will say it counted. Keep the first. Release the other for real — not because no one will notice, but because your hands are cleaner without a waiting thing clenched in them.

cells.tense: What you gave up is already behind you, and you stand at the door it closed.
cells.act: stand firm in the material hardship
cells.ask: Each day this week, stand in a hard fact of what you gave up, unmoving, for a short while — asking nothing back from it.
cells.core:
The sacrifice already happened. You stand where you set the thing down, still facing it, because moving on would mean it had no one to see it. That's not wrong of you. It's just a door you keep standing in front of. Nothing about what you gave up changed. The weight you feel is the room staying where it was.

Your own steadiness is what carries you, not news arriving. Pick a hard fact of what you put down and stand in it without flinching each day, letting it ask nothing of you. You have reserves enough for that. The standing is its own tending, and whether anyone claps is nobody's business but yours.

cells.tense: You keep giving things up for other people and calling it nothing much at all.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: When you quietly give something up for someone this week, name what you let go of to yourself in one plain sentence, then keep tending it.
cells.core:
You do this constantly. You step back and call it no big deal, you hand over your slot and say it suits you better anyway. What you actually did doesn't get named, not even inside your own head. The cycle keeps running and the one who gave keeps leaving the room before the toast. Nobody is taking credit. You're just handing it away.

Name it once, to yourself, before it drifts off. One plain sentence about what you let go of, in your own voice — not to claim anything, just so your own books show it happened. Then look after what you released the way you'd tend something you planted and mean to keep.

attempts.check: The record does not say who witnessed the sacrifice or whether anyone did; the draw only says the completing is external and shared, so I describe a person waiting for the cycle to close and never assert a witness existed. A reader could say the honoring already happened and this is just slow to land — the asks survive that, since sitting with a thing released, tending one small living thing, and stopping the proof are useful either way. The line that serves me more than the person is any phrasing that implies they were overlooked; I keep the lack of acknowledgment as location, not as an accusation.
